notes.meaning: The Sadducees asked Jesus who the woman would belong to in the resurrection, since seven brothers had married her on earth. They did not actually believe in life after death. They invented this extreme story to make the resurrection look foolish.

Jesus told the Sadducees that their thinking was completely wrong. They did not understand the true meaning of the Scriptures, and they did not understand the power of God. Because they doubted what God can do, they could not imagine life beyond the grave.

Jesus explained that when people rise from the dead, they will not marry or be given in marriage. In heaven, believers will be like the angels, living forever without death. Being like angels does not mean turning into angels, but sharing their deathless life where earthly marriage is no longer needed.

Jesus directed them back to the books of Moses, which the Sadducees accepted. At the burning bush, God called Himself the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob long after those men had died. God would not claim to be the God of people who were gone forever.

God is the God of the living, not of the dead. Because God keeps His promises to His people, the patriarchs are still alive to Him, and their bodies will one day rise. Jesus warned these leaders that their denial of the resurrection was a terrible mistake.

A scribe had listened to the debate and saw how well Jesus answered the Sadducees. He then asked Jesus which commandment was the most important of all. Jewish teachers often debated which laws were greatest, and this man came with an honest desire to learn.

Jesus answered by quoting the opening words of the Jewish confession of faith from Deuteronomy: the Lord our God is one Lord. Before giving a command, He reminded the scribe of who God is. True worship begins by recognizing that there is only one living God.

The first command requires loving God with the whole person. This means loving Him with sincere feelings, warm devotion, clear understanding, and every bit of our energy. When love for God fills the heart, it leads us to obey everything else He asks.

The second greatest command is to love our neighbors just as we love ourselves. We are called to treat other people with the same care and fairness that we want for ourselves. Jesus declared that no other commandment is greater than these two.

The scribe warmly agreed with Jesus and said He had spoken the truth. He confirmed that there is only one God and no other being beside Him. This teacher recognized that Jesus taught the heart of God's word accurately.

Loving God with all one's mind and strength, and loving one's neighbor, is far greater than all animal sacrifices. The scribe understood that God cares about inner love and obedience more than outward rituals. Sacrifices meant nothing to God if the person offering them lacked love.

Jesus saw that the scribe answered with real spiritual wisdom and told him he was not far from God's kingdom. The man understood the true spirit of the law, which prepared him to receive Christ. After this exchange, none of the leaders dared to challenge Jesus with trap questions.

differ.view: Understanding the law helps a person see their sin and need for Christ's mercy, which prepares them to enter the kingdom by faith rather than good deeds.
The scribe was almost a Christian, standing right at the threshold of faith, and likely went on to believe in Jesus.
The scribe was near to entering the visible church community on earth, which leads to heaven, though he still needed personal faith in the Messiah.
Being near the kingdom meant being close to the gospel age, but knowing the law cannot save anyone because salvation is entirely a gift of grace.

notes.meaning: While teaching in the temple, Jesus raised a question about the Messiah. The scribes taught that the Christ would simply be a descendant of King David. While that was true, their teaching missed the higher truth about who the Messiah really is.

Jesus pointed to Psalm 110, where David spoke under the guidance of the Holy Spirit. In that psalm, David recorded the Lord God speaking to David's Lord, inviting Him to sit at His right hand until His enemies were conquered. This proved that David himself recognized the Messiah as someone higher than an earthly ruler.

Jesus asked how the Messiah could merely be David's son if David called Him Lord. The answer is that the Messiah is both human as David's descendant and divine as the Lord of all. The large crowd heard this wise teaching with great pleasure.

Jesus warned the people to stay on guard against the scribes. These teachers loved to walk around in long, formal robes so others would think they were important. They used their position to draw attention and demand respect in public places.

These leaders loved getting the front seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at dinner parties. They cared more about human applause and high status than about serving God. Their religion was mostly a show to puff up their pride.

Behind their show of long prayers, the scribes cheated helpless widows out of their homes and property. They disguised their greed with a display of deep piety to take advantage of vulnerable people. Because they hid cruelty under the mask of religion, God will punish them far more severely.

Jesus sat across from the temple offering boxes and watched people putting in their gifts. Many rich people arrived and dropped in large sums of money. Jesus was observing not just how much was given, but the spirit behind the giving.

A poor widow came forward and put in two tiny copper coins worth only a fraction of a cent. Though her gift seemed almost worthless to others, it was all the money she had. Even with only two coins, she held nothing back.

Jesus called His disciples over to make sure they did not miss what the widow had done. He told them that this poor woman had put more into the treasury than all the wealthy givers. In God's eyes, the worth of an offering is measured by the love and sacrifice of the giver, not the size of the coin.

The wealthy gave out of their extra money that they would never miss, making no personal sacrifice. This widow gave out of her extreme poverty, placing into the offering all the money she had to live on for the day. Her quiet gift showed complete faith that God would provide for her needs.

differ.view: Rather than praising an example to follow, Jesus is pointing out a tragedy where a corrupt religious system pressured a destitute widow to give up her last bite of food.
